title: How wide are the angles in our classroom?
description: Angles around the classroom, such as the corners of a board and a book, are measured with a protractor. The centre goes on the corner, one edge goes on the zero line, and the number is read where the other edge crosses the scale.
teaching_notes: One idea: any corner can be measured by the same three checks of the protractor. Watch for students who place the protractor away from the corner and trust the number.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q2
video_script.why: The child measures real angles around the classroom by the three checks of the solved example.
video_script.substitution: The corners and edges of the classroom in place of the drawn angles.
video_script.anchor: a classroom with a board, a book, a door and a window, each corner marked with a small arc
video_script.payoff_line: The corners of a book and a board read about ninety degrees

final_answer.value: the corners of a book and a board read about a right angle; other angles read differently

maths_rules: the question is open-ended, so no single number is the answer
the corner of a book or a board is a right angle, which reads about 90 degrees
a door opened a little makes a smaller angle with the wall
the count starts at 0 on the edge that lies on the zero line
video_script.design: A classroom picture stays on the board. The protractor is placed on one corner by the same steps, and the right-angle reading is held back until the answer line.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, about angles in our classroom.
<bookmark mark='room'/>Look around, at the board, a book, the door and a window.
We have to measure the angles we find there.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Before we measure, which of these angles do you expect to be a right angle?

beats.on_screen: the classroom stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a protractor with its centre point and zero line marked, next to the corner of the board

marks.way: the protractor appears next to the corner of the board
marks.zero: the zero line lights up and the scale that starts there is circled

beats.colours: centre in gold, zero line in green
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We measure these the way the example in your book showed.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>The centre of the protractor goes on the corner.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>One edge goes along the zero line, and we read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: a classroom with a board, a book, a door and a window

marks.given: the four objects are listed under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a classroom with a board, a book, a door and a window.

beats.on_screen: To find: the degree measures of different angles in the classroom
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the degree measures of different angles in the classroom.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: choose an angle, such as a corner of the board; put the centre of the protractor on the corner

marks.centre: the protractor slides until its centre point meets the corner of the board
marks.why: a tick appears beside the centre point

beats.moves_through: the protractor slides onto the corner
narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, choose a corner of the board, and put the centre of the protractor exactly on it.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The corner is the vertex, and an angle is measured at its vertex.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: turn the protractor until one edge lies along the 0 line

marks.turn: the protractor turns until one edge meets the zero line
marks.scale: the scale that starts at that zero is circled

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns about the corner
narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, turn the protractor until one edge lies along the zero line.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>We read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the number on that scale where the other edge crosses it

marks.read: the other edge is followed out to the scale and the mark it crosses lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step three, follow the other edge out to the scale, and read the number where it crosses.
That number is the measure of the angle in degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: do the same for a corner of a book, the door and a window

marks.again: the protractor moves to the book, then the door, then the window

beats.moves_through: the protractor moves from one object to the next
narration: <bookmark mark='again'/>Step four, do the same three steps for a book, for the door, and for a window.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: compare each reading with a right angle; narrower reads less, wider reads more

marks.right: a right angle is drawn beside each reading
marks.check: a tick or a cross appears under each reading

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step five, compare each reading with a right angle.
<bookmark mark='check'/>An angle narrower than a right angle must read less. A wider angle must read more.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the corners of a book and a board read about 90°; the door and the window give other angles

marks.ans: the readings appear under the board and the book, and then under the door and the window

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The corners of a book and a board read about ninety degrees.
A door opened a little reads less, so every angle has its own reading.
